Subject: Quick recap + next steps from today's discovery

Hi Priya / Amit —

Thanks for taking time today. Short recap from my side so we all have shared context and clear next steps for the pilot discussion: 

Summary of pain & goals
- Pain: Production NLU/QA pipeline is brittle at scale; high per-query cost and latency spikes during end-of-quarter reporting windows.
- Goal: Reduce per-query cost by ~40% for bulk analytic prompts; keep 95th percentile latency under 300ms for single-turn queries.

Scope we discussed for a 6-week POC
1) Ingest a representative sample of your prompt set (approx. 25K queries/day peak).
2) Run generation and embedding workflows against two model variants (open base + Redwood-quantized).
3) Measure cost per 1k tokens, p95 latency, and answer-quality on a fixed eval suite.
4) Implement prefix/KV caching on repeated prompts and test effect on throughput.

Success metrics (proposed)
- Cost: >=35% reduction vs current baseline on same workload
- Latency: p95 <= 300ms for 1-2k token requests
- Quality: no more than 4% drop in core NPS-like accuracy on the eval set

Immediate asks (for access/setup)
- Provide a scoped dataset (S3 link or sample CSV): customer_example_prompts.csv
- Create a read-only service account (AWS IAM) for Redwood to pull data and push logs
- Add ben.carter@redwood.com to your Okta group for API key provisioning

I've attached a short draft charter and a checklist for infra access. Can you confirm the S3 path and the timeline for creating the service account? Once we have access, Ben will run a baseline pass and Sean will align on eval criteria.

Thanks —
Marissa
